scope: Supervised retirement of staged and obsolete boot files, initial production recovery-journal publication, and archival of the bootstrap reservation. Temporary-file tests only; no live privileged adapter, boot mutation or reboot ran.

validation.order: The full Rust suite preceded the final 1024-entry map bounds and bounded temporary-file capacity credit. Clippy, Rust 1.89 checks, formatting, AArch64 compilation and both selected 33-test runs used the final source. Yocto checks include the protocol-2 image identity.
validation.artifact_source: Debug binaries were built from the working tree subsequently committed as implementation_commit; they are not a clean packaged runtime image.

properties_exercised: Copy, publication, removal, directory-flush, recovery-handoff and reservation-archive interruptions reopen and resume from durable intent; canonical files and hostname retain bytes and inodes.
Missing, corrupt, linked or unexpected archive contents after archive completion stop progress without repair. Source and final guard changes cannot remove unarchived data.
Journal write, file-sync, rename and directory-sync failures preserve the active reservation until the exact initial production record is durable.
Retirement intent cannot be undone; later canonical failure requires the operator and cannot select the retired staged fallback. A new boot requires fresh health.
Completed bootstrap with missing or changed production state cannot be treated as fresh provisioning. Repeating completion preserves the initial recovery record inode.

Generation zero permits the first signed generation one without inventing release history. Unqualified hardware, generation-zero candidates, protocol-1 candidates and schema-1 recovery journals remain rejected.
The real AArch64 prepare, activate and finish commands reject UID 1000 before digest parsing or installed-path access.

pi5.denial: device mutations require the root-owned service

limits: Fixed-path root admission, FAT retirement, actual mount/service state and live production handoff have not run on either Pi.
Fixture interruptions and synthetic boot/health evidence do not qualify power loss, watchdog reset, firmware fallback or bad-root startup.
No installed Pi boot files, root partitions, production state, system bus or watchdog were changed; Pi 4 was not exercised in this validation.
A clean protocol-4 bootstrap / protocol-2 recovery image and new schema-3 kits are still required; older images and journals must not be relabeled.
Root connection details, independent backup/restore rehearsal, access closure, supervised trials and both-board physical qualification remain outstanding.
Feed publishing, download/service/radio/policy/UI integration and qualified rollout are still required before automatic updates work.
